researched.description: Wi-Fi-based space occupancy analytics and planning software for colleges and universities
researched.notes: Formerly Degree Analytics; rebranded to CampusIQ. Site footer shows the legal entity as MF Genius, Corp.

researched.description: Campus ID credentialing, tuition and dining payments, access control and foodservice software for colleges, universities and hospitals
researched.notes: Rebrand of Transact + CBORD, completed March 2026; a Roper Technologies subsidiary. transactcampus.com and cbord.com still redirect/coexist during the transition. Exhibited under the transitional 'Transact + CBORD' name.

researched.description: Financial close, consolidation and planning platform for large enterprise finance teams across all industries
researched.notes: Horizontal corporate performance management vendor (Nasdaq: OS) selling to Costco, UPS, Toyota et al.; higher ed and public sector are one of many verticals. Owner call.

researched.description: Digital textbook and courseware delivery platform used by colleges, universities and their publishers
researched.notes: Site blocks automated fetches (Cloudflare 403); details confirmed from Wikipedia, CB Insights and Library Technology Guides profiles. Judgment call: a large share of revenue comes from publishers rather than institutions directly, though inclusive-access programs are sold to campuses.

researched.description: Animal intake, medical, foster and adoption record software for animal shelters and rescue organizations
researched.notes: Buyer base is mixed: municipal animal-control shelters plus a large share of nonprofit foster-based rescues. No founding year found on the site or in Crunchbase-style sources.

researched.description: Localgov tax filing and revenue collection platform for municipal and county revenue departments
researched.notes: Localgov is Azavar's SaaS product; Azavar also runs a revenue/utility-tax audit consulting practice, so the company is part product, part services. Site claims 31 years serving communities but states no founding year, so year omitted.

researched.description: Continuing-disclosure repository and post-issuance compliance platform for municipal bond issuers and obligated persons
researched.notes: dacbond.com is an Angular app that returns no readable text to crawlers; confirmed via SEC comment-letter filings on DAC letterhead and GFOA's vendor listing. DAC is both a platform and a dissemination-agent service, formerly an Ernst & Young affiliate. No founding year confirmed.

researched.description: Fund accounting and ERP software for cities and local governments, covering financials, payroll, utility billing and municipal court
Performance-fee cost and vendor spend optimization engagements for large budget holders including city governments
researched.notes: Judgment call. Markets an AI 'Financial Intelligence Engine' but sells outcome-based savings engagements: their own pricing page says clients pay nothing if savings are not realized, with 'no consulting fees, no licenses.' Reads as an analytics-backed advisory firm, not a licensed product. Worth a second look if the owner counts outcome-priced analytics as product.

researched.description: Cloud customer information, billing and field service software for municipal water, sewer, electric and gas utilities
researched.notes: No founding year stated on the site. Category is the closest fit in the map: the product is a utility-wide CIS spanning water and electric, not grid hardware.

researched.description: Employee leave of absence and ADA accommodation management software for employers, TPAs and PEOs in all industries
researched.notes: Horizontal HR compliance software. Public employers (K-12 districts, higher ed) are two of five named verticals alongside healthcare and banking. Owner call.

researched.description: Open-source enterprise learning management and performance software sold across healthcare, government, retail and manufacturing
researched.notes: Horizontal LMS: government is one of eleven industries listed on their own site. Sold largely through a reseller/partner network. Owner call.

researched.description: Menu planning, production record and performance analytics software for K-12 school nutrition departments
researched.notes: menulogic-k12.com 301-redirects to menulogic.io. Site footer names the operating entity Foodworks Technologies, LLC. No HQ or founding year found on the site, Tracxn, or LinkedIn.

researched.description: Advanced metering infrastructure, distribution automation and grid data software for public power utilities and electric cooperatives
researched.notes: Publicly traded as Tantalus Systems Holding Inc. (TSX: GRID). Sells connected metering hardware alongside the software platform, but the platform is the primary offering.

researched.description: CIMS work order, asset and daily task management software for county road, highway and public works departments
researched.notes: Name collision resolved: several unrelated firms use 'Diversified Computer Services' (dcs-kc.com in Kansas City, dcsipros.com AS/400 accounting, dcrinc.net). The NACE exhibitor is the Montgomery, Alabama firm whose CIMS product is deployed in county road departments. DCS also sells managed IT services alongside its products; site claims 30+ years but states no founding year.

researched.description: Legal case and matter management software for prosecutors, public defenders, city and county attorneys, school districts and tribal governments
researched.notes: Acquired in 2024 by Waxman Ventures and rolled up with Judicial Dialog Systems (founded 1994) and Cycom Data Systems (founded 1984); HQ moved from the original Philadelphia location to North Canton, OH. Founded year 1989 is LegalEdge's own, from its About page.

researched.description: Family caregiver burnout assessment and care-plan platform for Medicaid agencies, area agencies on aging, health plans and long-term care insurers
researched.notes: Founding year not on their own site; 2014 is from CB Insights and PitchBook profiles, though one press interview describes a 2017 launch, so treat the year as soft. Delivery pairs the software with staffed care specialists.

researched.description: Fair-chance job matching and reentry platform for corrections agencies, probation and parole departments, reentry nonprofits and background-friendly employers
researched.notes: Acquired by Orijin; the site announces the combination into an education-to-employment pathway. Buyer mix is split between public agencies and private employers paying to post fair-chance roles. Crunchbase lists Columbus, OH; their own About page gives an Austin, TX address, which I used.

researched.description: Contingency management and recovery support software for substance use treatment providers, and PARCA supervision tools for probation and parole agencies
researched.notes: Straddles two categories: the criminal-justice product PARCA is why they exhibited at APPA, but the larger product line is behavioral health treatment software.

researched.description: Water data management and regulatory compliance software for water utilities, cities and environmental agencies
researched.notes: Operates as Aquatic Informatics ULC under Veralto Water Quality; acquired by Danaher in 2020 and carried into the Veralto spin-off. Products include Aquarius, WIMS, WaterTrax, Linko and Tokay.

researched.description: After-hours call intake, incident triage and crew dispatch software for water, sewer and electric utilities and public works departments
researched.notes: Category is a compromise: Daupler RMS is cross-departmental (water, sewer, stormwater, electric, general public works), and water/sewer is its largest market. Founding year from Crunchbase and the KCRise Fund portfolio page, not the company site.

researched.description: IoT sensor and AI wastewater monitoring platform that traces upstream pollution events for water authorities and treatment plants
researched.notes: Sells IoT hardware alongside the analytics platform. Founding year from Israeli startup press and Startup Nation Central, not the company's own about page.

researched.description: Reinforcement learning control software that automatically optimizes chemical dosing and process settings at drinking water and wastewater plants
researched.notes: The homepage is written generically about 'plants'; water and wastewater is confirmed as the actual market by their December 2024 $5M seed announcement (led by TQ Ventures) and WaterWorld coverage of deployments at three Alberta and BC plants. No founding year found.

researched.description: Cloud SCADA monitoring, alarming and analytics software for water and wastewater utilities, treatment plants and lift stations
researched.notes: Part of the MANN+HUMMEL Group. No founding year found on their about page or in Crunchbase.

researched.description: Subscription online training and CEU tracking platform for water and wastewater operators pursuing state licensure
researched.notes: HQ omitted deliberately: the .us site states no location, and ZoomInfo lists a Neuilly-sur-Seine, France address, which I could not corroborate against the US-facing business. Judgment call on verdict: this is a training-content subscription rather than an operational system, but it is delivered as a licensed e-learning platform, not a services engagement.

researched.description: AI talent intelligence and recruiting platform for large enterprises across technology, finance, pharma, telecom and government
researched.notes: Horizontal HR tech: named customers are Salesforce, Citi, HP, HSBC. They hold FedRAMP authorization and sell to state workforce agencies, which is why they exhibited at NASWA, but government is one vertical among many. Owner call.

researched.description: Registered apprenticeship and work-based learning management software for state workforce agencies, community colleges, school districts and employer sponsors
researched.notes: Acquired by WGU Labs in September 2024 and now runs as a nonprofit operating division of Western Governors University under the retained Craft Education name. HQ and founding year are from PitchBook and the WGU acquisition press, not the current site.

researched.description: Biometric identity verification, liveness and KYC platform sold to banks, fintechs, gaming, telecom, healthcare and government
researched.notes: Horizontal identity vendor. It has government-specific products (GovFaceMatch, state unemployment-fraud use cases) but its own industry list runs from crypto to dating apps. Owner call.

researched.description: Managed WebOps hosting and site management platform for WordPress and Drupal, sold to universities, agencies, brands and media companies
researched.notes: Legal name Pantheon Systems, Inc. Higher ed and government are two of seven verticals it lists alongside Home Depot and Clorox; The City of San Diego and Princeton are both named customers. Owner call.

researched.description: No-contract AI dashcam telematics and fleet tracking subscription for small and mid-size fleet operators
researched.notes: Name resolution: FLEETA is the fleet management service of BlackVue (Pittasoft), the Korean connected-dashcam maker, which is the entity that exhibited it at NAFA 2026 - not a standalone startup. HQ given is BlackVue/Pittasoft's; a separate US operating address was not found. Horizontal by design: the stated target is ELD-exempt local SMB fleets, with government fleets incidental. There is also an unrelated-looking fleeta.ai; the NAFA exhibitor is fleeta.io.

researched.description: IT service management, mainframe and IT operations automation software for large enterprises in every industry
researched.notes: Horizontal enterprise IT vendor, privately held by KKR. State government is a named vertical but a small slice of the business. Owner call.

researched.description: Agentless cloud security posture and workload protection platform for enterprises running AWS, Azure and Google Cloud
researched.notes: Google completed its $32B acquisition of Wiz in March 2026, so Wiz now sits inside Google Cloud - which strengthens the case that this is a big-tech horizontal rather than a govtech card. Owner call.

researched.description: Workforce and customer identity and access management platform sold to organizations in every industry
researched.notes: Horizontal identity vendor (Nasdaq: OKTA) with a FedRAMP-authorized public sector edition. Owner call.

researched.description: Cyber risk ratings and third-party attack surface monitoring for enterprises, insurers and government agencies
researched.notes: Horizontal ratings product used for vendor risk, board reporting and cyber insurance underwriting across all industries. Owner call.

researched.description: Cybersecurity program management and NIST CSF compliance platform for county governments and critical infrastructure agencies
researched.notes: HQ omitted: their own site gives no address, and ZoomInfo/The Org list only the region 'Lehigh Valley, PA' rather than a city, which does not meet the City, ST format. Purpose-built for the public sector - they run a County Government Cybersecurity Alliance and a HIPAA compliance push with NACo, which distinguishes them from horizontal GRC vendors.

researched.description: Child support lien network, new hire reporting and Medicaid recovery web systems for state child support and labor agencies
researched.notes: Their own site describes the company as a web systems builder for government, so part of the engagement is custom development; the lien network and new hire reporting products are recurring systems, which is why this reads as product rather than services.

researched.description: Gamified phishing simulation and security awareness training built only for K-12 districts, staff and students
researched.notes: Emerged from stealth in May 2024 with an $800k pre-seed and raised $5M in January 2026, but no incorporation or founding year is stated on the site or in the funding press, so the year is omitted. Category is a judgment call: this is cyber rather than physical safety, but School Safety is the closest bucket in the map for threat protection.

researched.description: IT help desk ticketing, device asset management and facilities service software built for K-12 school districts
researched.notes: Backed by JMI Equity (2021) and Cove Hill Partners (2024). Founded August 2016 per company and investor press; the platform launched publicly at ISTE 2017, so some sources cite 2017.

researched.description: Classroom browser monitoring, web filtering and student wellbeing alerting software for K-12 schools and districts
researched.notes: Now a business unit of Cordance Operations LLC, which is why the HQ reads Raleigh rather than the company's original New Zealand base. Founding year omitted: the only on-site signal is a '2010-' copyright range, which is not a stated founding date.

researched.description: Free keyboarding, digital citizenship and AI literacy curriculum for K-12 schools, with a paid ad-free district edition
researched.notes: Operated by Teaching.com (formerly FTW Innovations, renamed 2015). HQ omitted because sources conflict: one profile puts Teaching.com in San Juan, PR after a 2016 move from Los Angeles, while Tracxn lists El Segundo, CA. Category is the closest available - this is instructional curriculum, not district operations, and the map has no K-12 curriculum bucket.

researched.description: Network detection and response platform that flags confirmed network compromises, sold across education, banking, healthcare and government
researched.notes: The K-12 landing page in the candidate URL is a vertical microsite, not the company's focus: education is one of six industries Lumu lists, and much of its go-to-market runs through MSPs. Owner call.

researched.description: Consumer-permissioned income, employment and asset verification API for mortgage lenders, banks, tenant screeners and benefits agencies
researched.notes: Acquired by Checkr, announced August 2026 - so this card and the Checkr card in this batch are now one company; worth merging or cross-linking. Public sector (SNAP/Medicaid eligibility verification) is one of seven verticals, with mortgage lending the largest. Owner call.

researched.description: Background check, identity verification and continuous criminal monitoring platform for employers across all industries
researched.notes: Horizontal screening platform serving 140,000+ businesses from gig platforms to staffing. It entered the government market in August 2026 by acquiring Truv, also in this batch. Owner call.

researched.description: Goal-oriented coaching and case management software for workforce boards, TANF and SNAP E&T programs and college career centers
researched.notes: Very small company (roughly 6 employees per Tracxn). HQ and founding year are from PitchBook/Tracxn, not their own site. Named deployments include Michigan Works! Southwest and SEMCA.

researched.description: Tenant screening reports and FBI-channeled criminal background checks for public housing authorities and rental property managers
researched.notes: Judgment call worth a second look. The candidate URL nbinformation.com is their consumer-facing 'National Background Information' FBI-channeler brand; the company site is ncrcredit.com. Their own copy describes a screening service bureau reselling credit-bureau, eviction and criminal records rather than a licensed software platform, which is why this is supplier rather than govtech - but they are a real NAHRO/AHMA vendor with a housing-authority specialization, so the owner may want it counted. Site claims 25-30+ years but names no founding year; no HQ address published.

researched.description: TAAG resident services case management and HUD performance tracking software for public housing authorities and social service agencies
researched.notes: Rebranded from Designing Success Inc. in September 2023 and is now affiliated with MPACT Strategic Consulting. No founding year stated on their about page.

researched.description: AI platform that turns outside medical records, faxes and imaging into structured clinical summaries for specialty medicine practices
researched.notes: Y Combinator W24 company. Their site pitches specialty medicine and healthcare organizations generally, not public behavioral health specifically, so this is general healthcare AI that happened to exhibit at NatCon - flagging rather than deciding. Founding year omitted: Tracxn says 2024, CB Insights implies 2023, and the site states neither. There is also an unrelated attunementclinical.com (assessment tools for testing psychologists) - the NatCon exhibitor is attunement.ai.

researched.description: Healthcare SafetyZone incident reporting and patient safety risk management software for hospitals, FQHCs, long-term care and behavioral health providers
researched.notes: Real software (Healthcare SafetyZone) paired with a Patient Safety Organization advisory arm. Buyer base is healthcare providers of every type, public and private, so behavioral health is one segment rather than the focus. No founding year published; they claim four decades in healthcare risk management and 20 years of SafetyZone.

researched.description: Browser-based HIPAA-compliant telehealth video platform for individual clinicians, clinics and health systems
researched.notes: General-purpose telehealth used across all of healthcare, with behavioral health as one large user segment; not a public-sector product. Founding year is soft: their own who-we-are page dates the project to 2013 while CB Insights lists 2014.

researched.description: EHR, scheduling, billing and staff management software for Medicaid-funded IDD and home and community-based services provider agencies
researched.notes: Purpose-built for state Medicaid HCBS/IDD waiver programs, with per-state compliance pages, which is why this reads govtech rather than general health IT. No HQ or founding year found on the site or in Crunchbase-style sources.

researched.description: EHR, practice management and revenue cycle software for behavioral health, human services and IDD provider organizations
researched.notes: MedSuite is a holding brand over five acquired products - Brittco, Electrobills, EMR-Bear, Millin and Susquehanna - so the founding year of the group is not published. Sells RCM as a managed service alongside the software.

researched.description: Ambulatory EHR, practice management and revenue cycle software for 40+ medical specialties including behavioral health and community health centers
researched.notes: General ambulatory health IT: behavioral health and FQHCs are two of forty-plus specialties. Legal entity is NXGN Management, LLC (taken private by Thoma Bravo in 2023). Year 1974 is from their own site copyright line, which is the only date they publish. HQ omitted - the company runs remote-first and publishes no headquarters city.

researched.description: AI-native ProvenEHR clinical, scheduling and billing platform for behavioral health, IDD and physical therapy providers
researched.notes: Founded by Matthew M. Dorman, who previously founded Credible Behavioral Health. No HQ or founding year published on the site, and search budget was exhausted before I could check third-party profiles.

researched.description: Healthcare workforce training, compliance and competency assessment platform for hospitals, post-acute, home care and behavioral health organizations
researched.notes: Horizontal healthcare LMS serving roughly 13,000 organizations across every care setting; behavioral health and government health entities are two segments among many. No founding year on their about page.

researched.description: All-in-one phone, texting, scheduling and payments platform for small dental, optometry and medical practices
researched.notes: Legal name Weave Communications, Inc. (NYSE: WEAV). This is small-business practice communication software, heavily dental-led, with no public sector orientation - the weakest govtech fit of the NatCon exhibitors. Sector/category assigned only to satisfy the map. No founding year found before the search budget ran out.

researched.description: Early Literacy Station and AfterSchool Edge learning workstations preloaded with ad-free, offline early literacy content for public libraries
researched.notes: Judgment call: the purchase is a physical workstation, which edges toward equipment, but the value is the curated software library and the buyer is almost entirely public libraries. Their about page says founded 'in the mid-1990s' with no specific year, so the year is omitted.

researched.description: Print, copy, PC session and payment management software with self-service kiosks for public libraries, schools and municipal agencies
researched.notes: The https www subdomain 301-redirects to plain http comprisetechnologies.com. Ships payment kiosk hardware alongside the software. No founding year published.

researched.description: Research databases, ebook collections and discovery software licensed to public libraries, academic libraries, schools and healthcare organizations
researched.notes: HQ read from the structured-data block on their own site; no founding year is published on about.ebsco.com and the search budget was exhausted, so the year is omitted. A large share of the business is licensed content rather than software, and corporate/healthcare customers sit alongside libraries - a borderline case if the owner counts content aggregators.

researched.description: Sierra and Polaris integrated library systems plus the Vega discovery and patron engagement suite for public libraries and consortia
researched.notes: Ownership chain resolved: Innovative Interfaces was acquired by ProQuest in 2020, and ProQuest by Clarivate in 2021, so the PLA exhibitor is Clarivate's public library software line. The candidate URL was a 2020 acquisition press release; the live product site is iii.com. Card is written for the Innovative library-systems business, not for Clarivate as a whole - if the owner prefers to track the parent, this becomes a scope_review on Clarivate. No HQ or founding year published on iii.com.

researched.description: Event programming, room reservation and activity pass software for public library systems
Investment research, fund ratings and portfolio data sold to asset managers, advisors and institutions, with a library-facing Investing Center database
researched.notes: The candidate URL points at Investing Center, the one product public libraries subscribe to; the company itself (Nasdaq: MORN) is a financial data business where libraries are a rounding error. Sector/category reflect the exhibited product, not the company. Owner call.

researched.description: All-you-can-read digital newspaper and magazine subscription licensed to public libraries, schools, hotels, airlines and hospitals
researched.notes: Originally NewspaperDirect. Content licensing rather than software, and hospitality/airline customers sit alongside libraries - a borderline case on the same axis as EBSCO.

researched.description: Patron mobile apps, event and room booking and discovery websites for public libraries and library consortia
researched.notes: Legal name Solus UK Ltd.; the candidate URL wp.sol.us 301-redirects to www.sol.us. Offices in Scotland, Australia and the USA. No founding year published.

researched.description: Online language learning courses in 140+ languages licensed to public libraries, schools, government agencies and businesses
researched.notes: Sells across libraries, K-12, higher ed, US government language programs and consumers, but the buyer base is predominantly public institutions, which is why this is govtech rather than scope_review. Category reflects the exhibited library product.

researched.description: Mainframe encryption, password reset and storage administration utilities for enterprises in education, government, healthcare and finance
researched.notes: Horizontal z/OS systems software (MegaCryption, ReACT, WizDom). Universities are a customer segment, not the market. Owner call.

researched.description: LTI apps and LMS extensions - search, assessments, polls, journals - for Canvas, Brightspace, Blackboard and Moodle at universities and school districts
researched.notes: Mixes licensed products with custom development, hosting and curriculum services, so part of the revenue is services. Their about page claims 20+ years of LMS experience but states no founding year.

researched.description: Unified identity, privileged access and password management platform for mid-to-large enterprises in finance, higher education and manufacturing
researched.notes: Formerly Hitachi ID Systems, rebranded to Bravura Security after Volaris Group acquired it; their site dates the identity business to 1992. HQ read from the site's structured-data block. Horizontal IAM/PAM with higher ed as one vertical. Owner call.

researched.description: Global CDN, DDoS protection, zero trust networking and edge compute platform used by websites and applications in every industry
researched.notes: Big-tech horizontal (NYSE: NET). The candidate URL is their FedRAMP High government landing page, but this is internet infrastructure sold to everyone. Owner call.

researched.description: Integration platform and content services workflow software connecting campus systems for university enrollment, financial aid, alumni and HR offices
researched.notes: Legal name Constituo Software LLC. Built exclusively for higher education, with 50+ named institutional clients. No HQ or founding year published on the site.

researched.description: Cloud observability, log management and application performance monitoring platform for engineering teams in every industry
researched.notes: Horizontal observability vendor (Nasdaq: DDOG); education and government are two of nine industries it lists. Owner call.

researched.description: Contact center, IVR and video communication software for customer service operations across all industries
researched.notes: A division of Enghouse Systems Limited (TSX: ENGH); the 1984 date is the parent's founding. Horizontal contact center vendor - higher ed is one of many customer types. HQ omitted: enghouseinteractive.com sits behind a Cloudflare challenge and enghouse.com's contact page returned 403, so I could not confirm a city (the parent is Canadian). Owner call.

researched.description: AI federated search and content discovery platform that unifies scattered content into one index for associations and member organizations
researched.notes: Flagged rather than decided: they exhibited at EDUCAUSE, but their own site pitches associations and organizations generally, with no higher-ed-specific product. Operating entity is NotchPoint, LLC d.b.a. FUSE Next (formerly FUSE Search). Founding year omitted - the only signal is a '2006-2025' copyright range. No address published on their contact page.

researched.description: Program Evaluation System analytics on academic program economics, enrollment demand and job outcomes for college and university leadership
researched.notes: Their own copy calls Gray DI a 'data, software, and services firm', so advisory work sits alongside the PES subscription; the subscription is the primary product. Also sells College Companions (CoCo), an AI student support suite. No HQ or founding year published on the site.

researched.description: Enterprise content management, intelligent document processing and workflow automation software for large organizations in every industry
researched.notes: Horizontal ECM (OnBase/Alfresco lineage) with more than half the Fortune 100 as customers; government and education are two of a dozen listed verticals. Owner call.

researched.description: Game-based quiz and engagement platform sold in three separate lines to schools, to businesses for training and events, and to consumers
researched.notes: Genuinely ambiguous and worth the owner's ruling. Education (Kahoot! EDU) is a real institutional business sold to districts and universities, but the corporate line (Kahoot! 360) and the consumer line are comparably sized, which is why I flagged rather than called it govtech.

researched.description: Lucidchart and Lucidspark visual collaboration, diagramming and whiteboarding software for teams in every industry
researched.notes: Horizontal collaboration software; education and public sector are two of nine listed solution areas. Founding date from Wikipedia (December 2008); the company converted from Lucidchart, LLC to Lucid Software Inc. in January 2011, so some sources cite 2010 or 2011. Owner call.

researched.description: AI grading assistant and rubric-based assessment tool that generates per-student feedback for teachers and school leaders
researched.notes: Two mismatches worth a second look. First, they exhibited at EDUCAUSE (higher ed) but the site is written entirely for school principals and classroom teachers, so I categorized by the product as instructed. Second, the customer testimonials are from private schools and a Taiwan literature program, so the public-school share of their base is unclear. Footer copyright reads 2021 but no founding year is stated, so the year is omitted.

researched.description: Video capture, management and search platform for lecture recording and enterprise training
researched.notes: Closest call in this batch. Higher education is Panopto's anchor market and origin (Carnegie Mellon), but their own site now splits '2,000+ customers across higher education and enterprise' and lists aviation, energy, insurance, manufacturing and telecom. The owner may reasonably want this as govtech.

researched.description: Cloud virtual desktops and virtual computer labs that deliver licensed course software to student devices at schools and universities
researched.notes: Operating entity is eLumin LLC. HQ omitted deliberately: the site's contact and about pages return 403 to automated fetches, and the only location signal is a Northern Virginia phone area code, which is not evidence of a headquarters. No founding year published.

researched.description: Video-based oral examination platform that lets instructors verify authentic student understanding and deter AI-assisted cheating
researched.notes: Legal name Rhetorix Corp. per the site footer. Very early-stage: no HQ, founding year, customer list or funding history published, and the web search budget was exhausted before I could check third-party profiles.

researched.description: IT service management and enterprise workflow automation platform used by large organizations in every industry
researched.notes: Big-tech horizontal (NYSE: NOW) with a large FedRAMP public sector practice, but ITSM is sold to everyone. Their site returns 403 to automated fetches; details from Wikipedia. Owner call.

researched.description: Residence life and student housing management software covering applications, room assignment, billing and community programming for universities and colleges
researched.notes: Higher education is the anchor market, but StarRez has expanded into private purpose-built student accommodation, build-to-rent and co-living, so a growing share of the base is commercial landlords rather than institutions. Recently acquired College Pads for off-campus housing. Neither HQ nor founding year is published on their about or contact pages.

researched.description: No-code workflow automation and AI agent platform for security, IT, finance and operations teams at enterprises
researched.notes: Dual headquarters: Dublin is the European HQ and Boston the US HQ per their contact page; I used the founding location. Horizontal security automation - named customers are Coinbase, Databricks, Reddit and Snowflake, with public sector one of four listed solution segments. Owner call.

researched.description: AI tutoring, WCAG accessibility remediation and curriculum mapping tools that plug into an institution's LMS
researched.notes: Naming is inconsistent and worth a check before the card ships: the site brands itself ZaristAI throughout while the domain and contact email are aristai.io. Very early-stage - the only traction figure given is '100+ educators', and no founding year is published (the footer copyright reads 2026).
